messages:
marisa_sales: HarborTech POC - running into a dims/encoding mismatch on our embeddings endpoint and occasional 429s. They say their local vectors are 1024 but we require 1536. Can eng/supp help with quick triage? cc @oliver_se @nisha_support :hourglass: 

oliver_se: Thanks — can you paste the exact request + response they saw? Also are they hitting our hosted API or Dedicated?

marisa_sales: Hosted. They sent this curl and the raw response:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1536","input":"How do I connect my DB?"}'
```
Response:
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error":"vector_dims_mismatch","expected":1536,"got":1024}
```

nisha_support: Ok that lines up with an encoder mismatch — sounds like they precomputed with a different local model/tokenizer. Ask whether they're using sentence-transformers or a custom encoder library.

sam_ml: Likely they used a 1024-dim open-source encoder and then tried to compare against our 1536 model. Quick checks: have them call `GET /v1/models` to confirm available embedding models and dims. Also ask them to dump a single vector and print its length before indexing.

devon_runtime: FYI I see rate-limit spikes for that customer around 11:03 PST — lots of large batches (batch_size ~512). With 1536 dims their payloads hit our max_batch_bytes and the frontend returns 429. Suggest reducing batch_size to 128 or enabling streaming batch mode.

oliver_se: Marisa — can you ask them to run this minimal python repro and paste output?
```python
import requests
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings', json={"model":"rwd-embed-1536","input":"test"}, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer sk-REDACTED"})
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)
# also print len of the local vector if they have it: print(len(local_vector))
```

marisa_sales: Forwarded. They replied with this stack snippet from their indexing job:
```
File "index.py", line 42, in add_vectors
  index.add(np.array(vectors).astype('float32'))
ValueError: Expected 1536 columns, got 1024
```

sam_ml: Confirms precomputed vectors are 1024. Two realistic paths: (1) re-run embedding jobs using our rwd-embed-1536 API so everything is consistent, or (2) temporarily route their inference to an rwd-embed-1024 variant if they cannot re-embed now (but note model semantics/accuracy will differ). Recommend (1) for production.

nisha_support: For POC timeline, if they want zero rework we could stand up a compatibility route, but need infra approval for routing/quota. @devon_runtime any quick wins?

devon_runtime: We cannot trivially upsample 1024->1536 without model inference. Short-term: spin up an alias endpoint routed to rwd-embed-1024 and throttle them to avoid 429s. I can create the alias and quota in the next dev window (ETA ~4 hours). I'll need their account id and the dataset name.

oliver_se: Also note pricing — 1024-dim model is cheaper per unit. Sales: confirm with customer if they prefer less lift (route to 1024) vs better rerank quality (re-embed to 1536).

marisa_sales: Customer wants minimal work for now and is OK trying the routed 1024 endpoint. Can we also limit burst so they don't hit 429s again?

devon_runtime: I'll create a routed alias `harbortech-embeddings` -> rwd-embed-1024 with daily quota 100k requests and burst limit 300. Posting creds here once live.

deploybot: Alias harbortech-embeddings created and routed to rwd-embed-1024 (id: alias_98765) :white_check_mark:

marisa_sales: Thanks everyone — I'll send alias + usage guidelines to the customer and note that for production they should re-embed with rwd-embed-1536 or accept quality tradeoffs. I'll also update the SCC answers about data handling and share back any follow-ups.

nisha_support: I can handle the security questionnaire bits (token retention, PII guidance). Also remind them to reindex with the same model before GA. :memo:
